**Issue #4779 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4779: Patch: kept card scripts take their last version from the patch that ships them, so a patch shipped first never leaves one stale
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When a patch changes how a card behaves, the build keeps the card's old behaviour, so a replay of a game played before the patch plays back exactly as it happened. Each kept behaviour carries a label, typed by hand, naming the last version that still used it. When another patch ships while a change is waiting to merge, that label ends up one version too early. Replays of games from the version that shipped in between are then played back with the new behaviour. They no longer match the game as it was played, so they are refused.

This has been fixed by hand six times in the last eight days, and two cases are still wrong on `main` today. A replay of a game from one of those versions in which Speciesist's Cry ran is refused, because playing it back with today's Speciesist takes away a mana the real game never lost. After this change, the label names the change's own patch entry, and the patch tool works out the version when that entry ships, so the label can't go stale and nobody has to fix it again.

## Why

- **The rule.** R767000 says a replay folds under the scripts its version ran: "the kept one a game uses is the earliest kept at or after the game's version". `docs/ADDING_CARDS.md:230` tells the author to add `(ID, the newest shipped version, a fn that builds the old scripts)` to `KEPT_SCRIPTS`. The newest shipped version can change while the branch is being built or waiting in the merge queue: `patches-ship.yml` ships after every merge that touches `pending/`, often several versions at once (#4401 shipped v0.6.9b and v0.6.9c together, #4264 shipped five).
- **Re-key fixes in eight days:**
  - #4061 (2026-11-16, 35 files): #3951's rows.
  - #4090 (11-17): six blocks at once. It renamed 20 scripts' fns, and its `rust (classify)` step hit the 10-minute timeout twice, so the workflow's timeout had to be raised.
  - #4480 (11-22): re-keyed #4395's Shadowstep row (`history.rs:1191`).
  - #4505 (#4496, 11-22, 18 files): #4423's and #4469's rows (`history.rs:1230`, `:1285`).
  - #4521 (11-22, 38 files): #4440's rows. v0.6.9n "shipped while it sat in the merge queue".
  - #4630 (11-23): #4440 part 2's rows. v0.6.11c "shipped while it sat in the merge queue".
- **Two keys are still stale at `c474345f8f`:**
  - #4356 (Stinkyscape+ Balance Changes V, #4353) merged at 2026-11-21 03:28. The newest shipped version was then v0.6.8d (`git show 99bf500496^:crates/cards/patches/patches.json`), but its rows are keyed at v0.6.8b (`history.rs:1153-1170`). v0.6.8c and v0.6.8d ran the old scripts, and v0.6.8e shipped the new ones. #4668 later added a v0.6.8d row for Mend Projector only (`history.rs:1358`), because its own change made today's script read a `health` field those versions lack. Repeater v5, Silly Silas, Speciesist, Medina Enforcer, A Glimpse into the Endless Sea and Mindustrial Revolution still stop at v0.6.8b. R4353020 and R4353021 still say "Through v0.6.8b".
  - #4380 (Enormous Elderberry, #4350) merged at 07:07. The newest version was then v0.6.9 (the 04:04 cut, #4383), but its row is keyed at v0.6.8d (`history.rs:1177`; R4350000 says "Games of v0.6.8d and before"). v0.6.8e and v0.6.9 ran the old pricing.
  - Today, a v0.6.8d game in which one of those six cards acted, or a v0.6.9 game that Embiggened an Elderberry card, folds under the new script. It misses its recorded hash and is refused as `rules_changed`.
- **No check sees it:**
  - `patches check` only asks that each carried card has some script (`crates/tools/src/patches.rs:1864-1868`).
  - `cargo jackioh carried` fails only when a script panics on an old definition. Silently different play passes.
  - A pull-request check can't see the merge queue: `rust (classify)` runs only on `pull_request` (`ci.yml:664`), and #4521's and #4630's ships landed while those PRs were queued. The queue's `patches check` runs on a shallow checkout with no history to diff against.

## Proposal

1. **Key by the fragment.** A branch keeps a script under its own fragment's name instead of a version: `(ID, "fragment:stinkyscape-balance-changes-v", fn)`, the stem of its `crates/cards/patches/pending/<stem>.json`. Rows that already name a version stay as they are.
2. **Record the fragment on ship.** `patches ship` writes on each version it adds to `patches.json` the fragment that version came from (`"fragment": "<stem>"`).
3. **Resolve the key at build time.** `crates/cards/build.rs` carries that map into `history.json`, and the kept rows' keys are resolved once when `HISTORY` loads, before `covering_at` (`history.rs:1636`) reads them:
   - a `fragment:` key whose stem a shipped version names resolves to the version just before that one, so a fragment shipped second in a two-version ship resolves to the first;
   - a stem no shipped version names yet resolves to the newest shipped version, because every shipped version so far ran the kept script.
4. **Catch typos.** `patches check` fails a `fragment:` key whose stem is neither a file in `pending/` nor a shipped version's `fragment`. Without this check, a typo would read as pending forever.
5. **Docs and ruling.** `docs/ADDING_CARDS.md` §3 says to key a kept script by your fragment. R767000's key gets a ruling of its own from the issue's block, with its proving test and its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<issue>.md`.
6. **Fix today's two stale keys.**
   - Re-key #4353's six rows to v0.6.8d, as #4630 did for v0.6.11c, and update R4353020 to R4353025's "through" versions.
   - Re-key Enormous Elderberry's row to v0.6.9 and update R4350000 to match.
   - Pin both with `assert_kept_through` tests (`history.rs:1977`).

**Rejected alternatives:**
- `patches ship` rewriting the key literal in `history.rs` into a version. The ship PR would edit the lines that queued card PRs append next to, so the merge queue would hit conflicts.
- A `classify` check that a row the branch adds names the base's newest version. It never runs in the merge queue, where two of the six went stale, and every catch would still cost a re-key PR.
- Inferring the link from shipped `plays` and `changes`. Those lists are incomplete: v0.6.9m shipped #4423's Corpse Eater change but does not list `core-089`. A check built on them flags 116 of today's rows.

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/patches.rs`: `ship` writes `fragment`, and `check` validates `fragment:` keys. Tests go beside its ship tests.
- `crates/cards/build.rs` and `crates/cards/src/history.rs`: key resolution, the #4353 and #4350 rows, and tests.
- `docs/ADDING_CARDS.md` §3; `crates/tools/README.md`'s `patches` row.
- `spec/rulings/` (a new ruling beside R767000, plus R4350000 and R4353020 to R4353025), `spec/pending/<issue>.md`, SPEC §11.
- `apps/web/src/patches/source.ts`, only if `patches.json` entries are typed strictly enough to need the new field.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `fragment:` row whose stem is still pending covers every shipped version back to the card's previous row (test over a fixture history).
- [ ] After one `patches ship` run ships two fragments as V1 then V2, a row naming the second fragment resolves to V1, and a row naming the first resolves to the version before V1 (test in `patches.rs`).
- [ ] `patches ship` writes `fragment` on every version it adds.
- [ ] `patches check` passes on today's tree, and fails, naming the row, on a `fragment:` key whose stem names neither a pending file nor a shipped version.
- [ ] v0.6.8c and v0.6.8d fold Repeater v5, Silly Silas, Speciesist, Medina Enforcer, A Glimpse into the Endless Sea and Mindustrial Revolution under their v0.6.8b scripts, and v0.6.8e folds them under its own.
- [ ] v0.6.8e and v0.6.9 fold Enormous Elderberry under its kept script, and v0.6.9b folds it under its own.
- [ ] `docs/ADDING_CARDS.md` says to key by the fragment.
- [ ] The new ruling's note and test pass `cargo jackioh spec check`.
- [ ] Green: `cargo test -p jackioh-cards`, `cargo test -p jackioh-tools patches`, `cargo jackioh patches check`, `cargo jackioh carried`.

## Size and risks

Medium to large: about 15 files across the cards crate and the tools, with one new ruling. It spans crates, so probably `difficulty:hard`.

**Risks:**
- A wrong resolution changes which script old replays run. The tests pin both the shipped and the pending case, and the existing per-issue `assert_kept_through` tests hold today's literal rows. Every reader of a row's version, including the definition-keys test at `history.rs:1880`, must read the resolved one.
- Re-keying the two stale blocks refuses any v0.6.8d or v0.6.9 game that a build carrying the new script played before the next ship, the same trade #4630 accepted for v0.6.11c.
- A later part of a split patch that keeps a script needs a fragment of its own. `classify --claims` already asks for one whenever a card plays differently.
```
